d: BOW Updates, Call Recaps and Executive Summaries are written by the Sr AM. Jr AMs appear as owners of action items, not as authors.
ev: In the last month, every BOW Update and Call Recap on shared accounts was posted by a Sr AM.

d: Brief by AM tasks for Funnels & CRM, CRO and Landing Pages are owned by the Sr AM or co-assigned with the Growth Director.
ev: A Jr AM was co-assigned to a CRM Brief by AM, but the brief was written by someone more senior.

d: New batches start when a senior asks, not from the Jr AM reading the performance report.
ev: Typical prompt from a Sr AM: “let’s get the performance report and prep a new batch.”

d: New assets, awards or client changes are spotted by the Sr AM and handed down.
ev: A client award and a new site pop-up were both flagged by the Sr AM, who then asked the Jr AM to use them.

d: Uploads and client approvals sometimes need a senior push. Pending approvals end up in the Sr AM’s BOW Update.
ev: “Please upload asap” from a Sr AM, and “we need your approval on the batch” in a client update.

d: Replies are friendly and fast, but often end at “thank you” without a next step or ETA.
ev: Several threads close with “Perfect, thank you!” where the next step was implied but not stated.

d: The right people are not always tagged, so the Sr AM or PM misses context.
ev: Sr AM reminder on a thread: “don’t forget to tag me and the Jr AM.”

d: Ops has had to remind Jr AMs about task fields and required attachments.
ev: Ops posts to Jr AMs on ClickUp fields and attaching the PM analysis to Creative tasks.

d: Formats and placements are occasionally fixed after delivery.
ev: Assets had to be re-exported in 9:16 after they were shared.

d: Jr AMs ask who should own a task instead of routing it from a clear map.
ev: “Should I assign it to this person or to you?” on a copy-update task.

d: When a client challenges strategy, the Sr AM answers with platform logic and how success will be measured.
ev: A client pushed back on testing several avatars; the Sr AM replied with the reasoning and kill criteria.

d: Martech escalations and the KickOff-to-Game-Plan sequence are run entirely by the Sr AM.
ev: Onboarding tasks (KickOff, accesses, audits, Game Plan) are all assigned to the Sr AM.
